description:
A Characterful Two Bedroom Duplex Apartment within a Landmark School Conversion

Description

Set within an impressive former school building, Flat 3 The Old School is an elegant two bedroom duplex apartment that blends historic architecture with modern design. The building dates back to the late nineteenth century and was originally constructed to serve the local community as a school, before being thoughtfully converted into a small collection of distinctive homes. Many original features remain, giving the property a sense of scale and character that is rarely found in modern developments.

The apartment offers exceptional open plan living and entertaining space, centred around a striking reception room with a dramatic double height ceiling and large windows that flood the space with natural light. The sleek open plan kitchen sits comfortably within the room and is ideal for both everyday living and entertaining.

The principal bedroom is arranged on a mezzanine level and benefits from fob entry access, excellent natural light and a real sense of privacy. A second generous bedroom is located on the lower level and offers built in storage along with direct access to the private garden. The smart bathroom is finished with a modern white suite.

Further benefits include a secure fob entry system, private off street parking and a secure private garden, making this a highly practical and desirable home in a prime Islington setting.

Location

The property is ideally positioned on York Way in the heart of Barnsbury, with an excellent range of local amenities right on the doorstep. Kings Cross is approximately 0.7 miles away and offers an outstanding choice of shops, restaurants, bars and cultural attractions, including Coal Drops Yard. Upper Street is around 1 mile away and provides further dining, shopping and entertainment options.

Transport links are excellent, with Kings Cross St Pancras station approximately 0.7 miles from the property, providing access to multiple Underground lines, National Rail services and international connections via Eurostar. Caledonian Road Underground station is roughly 0.4 miles away, offering easy access to the Piccadilly line. Several bus routes also operate along York Way, connecting the area to the City, West End and beyond.

Square Footage: 990 sq ft

Additional Info

Islington is popular with young professionals and families alike. A wide assortment of accommodation, streets and green areas make for a stimulating environment while excellent eateries, art and culture add to the variety and vitality of the area.

Much of the area including Barnsbury, Canonbury and De Beauvoir Town was developed in the Georgian and Victorian eras and retains many of the original architectural features of those times. The grand residential homes, courtyards and squares across the district have established Islington as a premier address in London.

Islington benefits from some spectacular parks and city gardens. Highbury Fields, situated just to the east of Highbury Gardens, is the largest open space in the borough of Islington. Across its 29 acres there are recreational facilities including eight tennis courts, a café, swimming pool and a football court at the north end.

The park is surrounded by highly desirable residences. Islington has some fantastic local theatres including the Almeida, a local award-winning 325 seat theatre, producing a diverse range of British and international drama with some of the world’s best artists, and has developed a worldwide profile. The King’s Head theatre, known for its music, has been a hotbed of new and exciting creative talent for more than 35 years. Not forgetting Sadler’s Wells, the UK’s leading dance house, uniquely dedicated to bringing the very best international and UK dance to London audiences.

All this culture and diversity attracts residents of a particularly discerning nature. Its close vicinity to the City, efficient transport links and the unique charm of Upper Street with its blend of cultural offerings and diverse shopping choices add further appeal.

Forest Hill train station is served by the London Overground (Orange Line) and Southern Rail. Travel times to central London stations include:

SHOPPING, DINING OUT AND RECREATION

As well as having a Sainsbury’s in both Forest Hill and Sydenham, Forest Hill is well served with a variety of high-quality independent shops. There are also gastro pubs, a gym, cafe´s, delis and restaurants to name but a few of its excellent amenities.

Some of our favourite local eateries span across both Forest Hill, Honor Oak and Sydenham and include Miss Margarita and Bona (sour dough pizza restaurants), Canvas and Cream (great local cafe´ serving a selection of cakes, food and drink. They also host some art exhibitions) and the award-winning Babur Indian restaurant.

Off the high street in the town centre, you'll find Forest Hill pools and library both of which have undergone refurbishment and located at the end of Thorpewood Avenue.

Forest Hill pools is known for its swimming pool facilities but is also a local leisure centre with a gym and fitness classes.

The Horniman Museum and Gardens is a well-known local point of interest and can be found just beyond Forest Hill town centre. It’s recognized as a popular family entertainment venue and has been featured in "Time Out". With regular events such as a farmer’s market, live music and seasonal festivals to name a few, there is always something to enjoy at the Horniman.

Alongside the Horniman, other local attractions include One Tree Hill at the top of Honor Oak Rise and offers some of the most breath-taking views across London and the city skyline. In our opinion this is a hidden gem.

Refurbished in 2006, the “Green Flag awards” winning park offers a children’s playground, an excellent cafe, and a popular cycle hire outlet. The Francis Peek centre has a varied programme of activities to suit everyone.

Sydenham Hill Woods is where you will find the highly acclaimed Cox’s Walk (an avenue through the woods created in 1742 by publican Francis Cox) is another amazing landmark in proximity of the house. The Woods are a unique mix of new and ancient woodland, with remnants of Victorian gardens and is London Wildlife Trust’s oldest nature reserve. Made up of approximately 11 hectares, Sydenham Hill Wood forms part of the largest remaining tract of the old Great North Wood. The wood is home to more than 200 species of trees and plants as well as rare fungi, insects, birds and woodland mammals. In the 1980s, Sydenham Hill Wood was saved from development threats, a testament to the determination of local people to safeguard nature. It became London Wildlife Trust’s first nature reserve in 1982 and Cox’s Walk came under the Trusts management in 1998.

Tucked behind Sydenham Hill Wood you will find yet another great attraction. The ever-popular Dulwich & Sydenham Hill Golf Club, which was founded in 1894. The golf course was designed by the great Harry S Colt and is set among mature oaks on the slopes of Sydenham Hill overlooking Dulwich College and enjoys a deserved lofty status among the capital’s golfing elite.

Lordship Lane Dulwich offers a vast array of popular gastro pubs, well-established cafes and restaurants, highly acclaimed local independent businesses such as butchers, cheesemongers, fishmongers, wine and craft beer retailers to name but a few. It has an abundance of indie shops and its trendy, easy-going vibe is extremely sought after. With a Picture House cinema, Lordship Lane is famed as the home of famous children’s writer Enid Blyton who was born at number 354. A blue plaque marks the spot. Today it is a hardware store, but Lordship Lane is still a great place to head to with a bunch of adventurous friends for great food and drink culture.

If you ever desire a further choice of drinking and eating establishments, the vibrancy of Dulwich Village can be found a walk or bus ride away. Dulwich Village is a charming historical village which was given conservation status in 1968. This upmarket area of South East London oozes charm and appeal. Highly acclaimed for its art gallery, green spaces and Belair House (a popular restaurant, wedding and events venue), Dulwich Village continues to entice high net worth individuals and families due to the varied and substantial family homes on offer and its world class schools.

If that wasn’t enough, Crystal Palace Park is an English Heritage Grade II listed park which has been renovated is also accessible form the property. It is said to be one of the largest parks in South London and one of the most significant in Britain. It is home to the National Sports Centre, and offers a number of recreational activities and a variety of heritage features including, Italian terraces, café, children's play area, former boating lake, maze, fishing lake, concert bowl, children's farm and the highly acclaimed and wonderful Crystal Palace Park dinosaurs.

The ground floor offers a particularly flexible layout, with a spacious kitchen/diner providing an excellent hub for family life and entertaining, alongside a separate lounge and sitting room. There is also a further kitchen/dining and living area within the annexe accommodation, together with a shower room, utility room and workshop/store, making the property exceptionally versatile for a large or extended family, those working from home or anyone requiring separate living space.

The driveway is enclosed by a controlled electric gate, offering an added level of security, privacy and convenience while also creating an attractive approach to the house.

Positioned in the middle of Fernbrook Road (a charming residential street in the heart of 'the posh side' of Hither Green!) sits this character-filled home boasting three double bedrooms, yet still with potential to extend.

Dating back to 1901, the property blends turn-of-the-century Victorian & Edwardian period architectural details with thoughtful modern improvements.
Having been Sam and her family’s first owned home, now for over 30 years, the property has been continuously enhanced and adapted to what it is today.

Originally recommended to Hither Green by a friend, the family were immediately drawn to the beautiful streetscape, and the home’s remarkable "tardis-like" feel compared to the other houses they'd seen. Modest from the road, yet opening up into surprisingly deep and generous living spaces inside.
While refurbishing, the family found a home packed with original soul - including slate fire surrounds, intricate cornicing, corbels, ceiling roses, and rich timber finishes, all of which they've subsequently worked hard to restore.

Coupled with fast connections into Central London (direct trains, just 15 minutes to London Bridge) and space to grow into long-term - Sam knew this place was for them.
Improvements Sam has made
Over her ownership, Sam has updated, maintained, and expanded the property to create a modern, energy-efficient, and versatile family home.
Since purchasing, upgrades include:
A ground-floor kitchen extension encompassing the former outbuilding area to create a more generous culinary space
A full loft conversion (completed Nov 2023) featuring a walk-in wardrobe (which was also plumbed ready for an en-suite if required)
Complete roof replacement across both the main structure and outrigger section with improved insulation
Installation of a modern roof window as a nod to the original period skylight
Restoration of the original wooden sash windows
A fully modernised family bathroom featuring a walk-in shower and freestanding bath
Rewired electrical socket system and upgraded consumer unit
Complete damp-proofing treatment on the ground floor
Rear garden transformation, de-concreting the space to lay a stone patio dining area and lawn
The Layout & Living Space
Definitely best viewed on our 3D model (our photos don't do the space justice!) the ground floor has been designed to retain classic period proportions while adapting comfortably to modern family life.
The Edwardian square bay window in the front reception allows for more furniture layouts (compared to 1930s curved bays), alongside an original slate fireplace, detailed ceiling rose, and restored cornicing. A separate formal dining room provides quiet separation for evening meals or working from home.
To the rear, the extended kitchen creates a natural focal point for everyday living, opening directly onto the private paved patio, and in the summer months, a gentle through-breeze keeps the entire ground floor naturally cool and fresh.

Unlike a lot of the competing houses locally, this home still offers potential to do a side return or further rear extension if required.
Across the upper floors, the bedrooms offer exceptional flexibility - two huge doubles and one normal double. The loft conversion serves as a quiet retreat for Sam's now adult son Ryan, complete with a walk-in wardrobe and elevated views of the surrounding area. Some in the area have extended above the first floor bathroom (should you need even more space up here).
The Great Outdoors
The rear garden offers a private, sunny haven designed for low-maintenance relaxation. The family removed the crude former concrete patio, to install a paved patio for outdoor dining flanked by a lovely lawn.
To the front, the property features a sheltered recessed porch as a safe discreet nook for parcel deliveries out of public view.
The Hither Green Lifestyle
Fernbrook Road is ideally positioned to enjoy the close-knit, vibrant atmosphere that Hither Green is now renowned for. From seasonal community gatherings in the park to Christmas celebrations at the station, the area maintains a lovely community feel.
For commuters, transport links are fast and convenient via Hither Green Station (an interchanging hub with two separate connecting lines):
12 to 15 minutes direct trains to London Bridge and Charing Cross
Direct services to Waterloo, Cannon Street, Blackfriars, and Victoria (via a quick switch at Lewisham)
DLR connections from Lewisham (a nice walk or 1-stop train ride), reaching Canary Wharf, and even London City Airport in 35–45 minutes
Convenient road and cycle routes to Greenwich Park and Blackheath
Some great green spaces surround the property. Manor House Gardens is just a 6-minute walk away (according to Google - 5mins if you ask Sam!), featuring a central lake with nesting swans and herons, tennis courts, open-air cinema nights, and a popular park café. Manor Park mixes it up with a gentle walk along the River Quaggy, ideal for young families.
Families are particularly well catered for, with three "Outstanding" rated primary schools nearby, including Brindishe Manor School situated on the adjacent road - a key reason why many families move into the area.
A curious piece of heritage: the original property deeds include a historic covenant stipulating that no pigs or pig products may be sold from the premises - a reminder of the area's agricultural history... you've been warned!

Here is a little more from Sam (the owner) directly:
What is the best thing about living on Fernbrook Road?
Simply the house... its space & flexibility; each room has been used in different ways over the years according to our needs. The neighbourhood & neighbours; having a lovely community feel (local community events in the park / at the station at Christmas etc). It's cool in summer and warm in the winter. The location; we can get to most places in London in minutes (London Bridge in 15 mins & Charing Cross 20/25 mins). Finally, having a lovely community school in the next road was a dream as young parents.
Why are you selling?
After 30 wonderful years raising our family here, we are ready for our next chapter and will rent in Whitstable where some of our family are. We're sad leaving behind a home and street we have loved deeply - if only we could pick it up and take it with us!

How are your neighbours?
We have fantastic neighbours all around us. Everyone looks out for each other - taking in parcels, feeding pets when away, and sharing Christmas drinks together. It’s a genuinely warm and friendly street, but equally accepting if any one wants to simply keep themselves to themselves.

What are the best local green spaces?
Manor House Gardens is our fave – such a lovely children’s play area, all the sports courts, a lake with fountain, and plenty of wildlife. It hosts cinema nights and sports days, and offers a lovely café and a designated 'dog-off-lead' area. It’s a special place for us, and the first place we took our Ryan from the hospital as a baby.
Blackheath – Great for cycling, with direct access to Greenwich Park, offering vast open spaces just minutes away.
Manor Garden – A hidden gem with access to a tiny river where children love to splash and play.
Best local Café?
Arloe & Mo – quirky & delicious food freshly cooked (amazing Guinness cake) and we never feel rushed.
Great Coffee from Bolla Bolla (a pop up at the station entrance). Sweet guy who runs it. If you’re early for your train, take a seat in a deckchair to enjoy your brew.
Best local pubs?
The Northbrook; great Sunday lunch (if you can get in!) & lovely beer garden. Large airy and spacious pub, with disabled access.
The Station (literally around the corner) has a really cool outside courtyard which is buzzing in the summer.
Best local restaurants?
Fera – Great for takeaway too (grilled salmon is fab!...as are their potatoes)
Cafe Green – Vietnamese fresh & according to those in the know very authentic.
Yard Sale Pizza – quick easy & a very short walk away
Casa Linda – lovely local Italian. Great pasta dishes & some lovely specials (inc great simple but fresh fish dishes)
Panas & Spice of Life – Indian restaurants on Lee High Road... so walkable. Had many a birthday celebration in Panas.
Manor Fish Bar – A truly eclectic take on fish & chips as the cover everything from halloumi & salads to battered sausage
… and loads more in Blackheath.

A fine example of the enduring transitional style, this fantastic two-bedroom apartment sits on the lower-ground floor of a handsome Victorian terrace in Kennington. Meticulously designed by Azman Architects, the flat's Victorian façade belies the modern lines and rich textural layering within. Arranged on split levels to create a sense of continuity, the generous south-facing garden stretches out at the rear with distinct seating areas that capture changing light levels.

The Architect

Radcot Street was reimagined by Azman Owens Architects, founded in 1993 by Ferhan Azman; the practice behind the Alexander McQueen flagship store on Conduit Street and the Vivienne Westwood Retrospective at the V&A. An award-winning architect and furniture designer, Azman is best known for her bold, clean-lined contemporary forms that are at once sensitive to the home’s period pedigree and strikingly distinctive.

The Tour

Behind its elegant London stock-brick façade with red-brick detailing lies a refined contemporary home. Positioned down a short flight of stairs, the dark-painted front door opens to a bright hallway with storage cupboards at its foot.

A seamless flow runs through a neat integrated workspace and continues into a spacious kitchen-living room at the far end with Havwoods engineered oak underfoot (fitted with underfloor heating). A pared-back colour palette washes the room, allowing the natural light drawn in through bi-folding doors to the garden to take precedence.

The kitchen is wonderfully streamlined with a run of crisp white cabinets and hardwood worktops. Appliances include a Smeg Pyrolytic Pizza oven, an induction hob, a Bosch dishwasher, and a separate fridge/freezer. There is space for a dining table, and the natural continuation to the garden invites outdoor dining in warmer months. A built-in speaker system has been installed here and throughout the flat.

There are two bedrooms. The first is at the front with a view out onto the street, while inward views are concealed with frosted glass. Original shutters invite restful sleep, and a wall of bespoke joinery provides plenty of storage. In the second bedroom, a study area has been thoughtfully positioned beneath a rooflight.

Just off the hallway, a bathroom includes a bath with an overhead shower, mosaic wall tiles and a heated towel rail.

Outdoor Space

Floor-to-ceiling glazed doors open onto a landscaped south-facing garden. Carefully positioned on split levels, there are two seating areas, flanked by mature hedging and a patinated brick wall. The garden is well-sized for entertaining with a connection to the kitchen, and there is a shed for outdoor storage.

The Area

Radcot Street is well-positioned just moments from the leafy green space of Cleaver Square and Kennington Park. The neighbourhood is peaceful, renowned for its elegant Georgian terraces and Victorian architecture.

A short walk away, Kennington Cross has an excellent selection of independent cafes, bakeries, pubs, and restaurants. Local favourites include Vanilla Black, Sally White, Urban Botanica, and The Prince of Wales pub. For arts and culture, the Newport Street Gallery in Vauxhall, the Imperial War Museum, and the Southbank Centre are all within easy reach.

Transport links are exceptional. Kennington Underground Station (Northern line) is just a few minutes’ walk away, with connections to the City, the West End, and beyond. Vauxhall Station (Victoria line and National Rail services) is also within comfortable walking distance, as are numerous bus routes serving central London.

description:
A beautifully presented two bedroom Victorian conversion in the heart of Dalston, arranged over three floors with two bathrooms and utility room. The generous layout gives each part of the home its own space, while Dalston’s independent food spots, pubs and cultural venues are all close by.

IF YOU LIVED HERE…

Your entrance is on the second floor, where there’s a separate utility room before stairs lead up to the main living level. Here, the kitchen and reception room is bright and open, with warm wood flooring and two large sash windows. Sleek white cabinetry keeps the kitchen simple, while there’s plenty of room for a dining table and seating. A bathroom with a bath and shower above also sits on this floor.

The first bedroom is particularly generous, with soft carpet, a large sash window and space for furniture beyond the bed. From here, stairs lead to a separate study, giving you a useful workspace away from the main living areas.

Up in the loft, the second bedroom stretches across much of the top floor, with wood flooring, a rooflight and its own ensuite shower room. There’s fitted storage along the eaves, as well as further built-in cupboards, making good use of the space beneath the roofline. Across all three floors, white walls, natural wood and plenty of daylight give the interiors a calm, cohesive feel.

WHAT ELSE?...

-Dalston is right on your doorstep, with Ridley Road Market, Dusty Knuckle, Oren and Mangal among the neighbourhood’s many places to eat, drink and shop, while Stoke Newington is also close by for Church Street and its independent cafés, restaurants, pubs and shops.

-For green space, Hackney Downs is close by, while London Fields and its lido are also within easy reach.

-Dalston Kingsland and Dalston Junction Overground stations provide excellent connections across east and north London, with plenty of local bus routes nearby too.

-Families are particularly well served by a great choice of highly regarded schools nearby.

-Ongoing council initiative to develop the former Colvestone Primary School building into a creative community hub, and a street greening plan that will include a dedicated pedestrian and cycle zone.

"We have been living on Colvestone Crescent for 20 years and love our home and the area. The whole flat was redesigned with architect Michael McNamara (LaMa Studio) to convert the loft space into a unique living and work space, with aerial views of the gardens and nearby St Mark church. Our other favourite part of the renovation is the mezzanine in the second double bedroom. Of course, it’s also a great street and area. There is a thriving community on Colvestone Crescent and everything Dalston has to offer on our doorstep. Yet, because it’s a no-through road, the flat is peaceful and quiet. This has been the perfect home for us to grow in. From our early days hosting dinner parties and film screenings, to our family home and the place where our two children are flourishing. So, whilst it’s time to move on, we will honestly miss it.”

description:
This stylishly extended detached house in Burpham offers well-presented and versatile family accommodation, combining a traditional brick exterior with a thoughtfully modernised interior. The property has been carefully updated to create bright, contemporary living spaces while retaining a warm and homely feel throughout. To the front, there is a driveway providing off-road parking and an attractive lawned frontage.

At the heart of the home is an impressive open-plan kitchen and dining space, created as part of the extension. The room is exceptionally light, with multiple rooflights and large glazed doors overlooking the garden. The contemporary kitchen features striking blue cabinetry, contrasting white worktops and a central island with breakfast seating, while the adjoining dining area provides an excellent space for family meals and entertaining. There is also a separate utility room and a useful family room, offering flexibility for modern family life.

The principal reception room is a spacious sitting room with a large bay window fitted with plantation shutters, allowing plenty of natural light into the room. A fireplace with a wood-burning stove provides a cosy focal point, complemented by built-in shelving and cabinetry. There is also a separate study, ideal for home working, along with a further reception/bedroom space that could be used in a variety of ways depending on the needs of the household.

Upstairs, the property provides four bedrooms, giving the house excellent family accommodation. The bedrooms are individually styled and benefit from plenty of natural light, with built-in storage available in several rooms. The accommodation is served by a well-appointed family bathroom with a bath and separate shower, while there is also a further shower room and a downstairs cloakroom. The interiors combine neutral tones with carefully chosen colours, feature wallpapers and contemporary fittings, giving the house considerable character.

One of the property's particular features is the generous rear garden. The garden offers a substantial area of lawn surrounded by mature planting, trees and established borders, creating a private and leafy setting. A paved terrace immediately adjoining the house provides space for outdoor dining and seating, while the garden extends beyond this into a more natural landscaped area. A stream runs through the garden, adding a particularly attractive and unusual feature, with planting and raised beds creating a tranquil, established feel. There is also a garden shed and plenty of scope for enjoying the outside space.

Overall, this is a characterful and substantially improved detached family home in Burpham, combining stylish contemporary accommodation with generous living space, four bedrooms, excellent flexibility and a particularly appealing rear garden with its own stream.

The Home -

Set within the distinctive Red Square development on Piano Lane, this exceptional two-bedroom duplex apartment offers a refreshing approach to modern London living. Behind the building's striking red façade and industrial-inspired architecture lies a home that celebrates colour, creativity and thoughtful design.

Arranged across the ground and first floors, the apartment extends to approximately 1,068 sq ft, with generous open-plan living spaces, two double bedrooms, two bathrooms and a private outdoor terrace.

Set within a gated development, Red Square offers a sense of privacy and security, with a concierge service adding convenience to everyday living.

Throughout, a confident mix of rich colours, natural materials, geometric patterns and carefully curated details creates an interior that feels both playful and considered. From the beautiful parquet flooring and sculptural staircase to the jewel-toned kitchen and individually designed bathrooms, every space has its own distinct character while remaining part of a cohesive whole.

Piano Lane is positioned in a vibrant pocket of Hackney, within easy reach of Stoke Newington, Dalston and Newington Green. The surrounding neighbourhood is known for its independent spirit, with an ever-changing collection of cafés, restaurants, creative businesses and local shops.

The Indoors -

The ground floor is arranged around an impressive open-plan kitchen, dining and reception space, extending to almost 28 feet in length. Beautiful herringbone parquet flooring introduces warmth and texture, while soft blush walls provide a calm backdrop for an eclectic collection of artwork, vintage furniture and contemporary design pieces.

The living area is wonderfully inviting, with a deep green velvet sofa, colourful rugs and statement lighting creating a relaxed setting for everyday life. Large glazed doors at the rear draw natural light into the space and open towards the private terrace, allowing the indoors and outdoors to connect naturally.

An architectural timber staircase rises through the room, its open treads and pale mint-green balustrade bringing a sculptural quality to the interior. Beneath, a dark feature wall provides a striking contrast to the lighter finishes, while thoughtfully arranged storage and furniture make excellent use of the space.

The kitchen is a particular highlight. Deep forest-green cabinetry is paired with beautifully veined pale worktops, brass hardware and rich emerald-green glazed tiles. A cream Smeg oven, traditional-style ceramic sink and open shelving introduce a charming mix of contemporary and nostalgic details, while a breakfast peninsula creates a sociable connection with the adjoining living space.

Beyond the kitchen, a further reception room currently serves as a creative studio, offering a wonderfully flexible space for working from home, making art or simply enjoying a quieter retreat. Black-and-white chequerboard flooring brings a graphic quality to the room, complemented by colourful cabinetry, display shelving and a glazed partition that allows light to travel through the ground floor.

Upstairs, two generously proportioned double bedrooms offer contrasting yet equally inviting spaces.

The principal bedroom is finished in a soft sage-green palette, with beautiful parquet flooring, a cane headboard and carefully chosen lighting introducing a sense of warmth and calm. A broad corner window brings in natural light, while a dedicated dressing area provides a practical addition. An adjoining en-suite shower room is lined in glossy blush-pink tiles, complemented by black-framed glazing, dark brassware and a sculptural white basin.

The second bedroom takes a more playful approach, with bold striped wallpaper, warm ochre tones and a deep blue feature wall. Two rooflights illuminate the room, while textured wall detailing, colourful artwork and built-in storage give the space a wonderfully individual character.

A further bathroom is a striking exercise in colour and material. Deep bottle-green glazed tiles wrap around the walls, contrasting with a black-and-white chequerboard floor and warm brass fittings. A freestanding white bathtub forms the centrepiece, creating an inviting space to unwind, while a separate shower adds everyday practicality.

Throughout the apartment, an expressive collection of lighting, artwork and decorative details brings a distinctive personality to the interiors, making this a home that feels genuinely individual.

The Outdoors -

A private terrace extends from the main living space, offering a secluded spot for morning coffee, outdoor dining or an evening drink.

Enclosed by pale timber fencing, the terrace has been thoughtfully arranged with built-in bench seating, timber decking and a decorative bistro table. Festoon lighting and a large industrial-style mirror add character, while the intimate proportions create a welcoming outdoor retreat away from the surrounding city.

Loving The Location -

Piano Lane is a quiet, residential street perfectly located within minutes of Stoke Newington, Clissold Park and Newington Green. At the heart of Newington Green is a four-way junction where Stoke Newington, Canonbury, Dalston and Green Lanes meet. Residents love Newington Green because of the close community and village atmosphere. Plenty of tree-lined residential streets just off the main thoroughfare lead to a plethora of fantastic cafes, bars and restaurants, some of the highlights include the ever popular Jolene, Yield wine bar and the lady Mildmay pub. If you like to eat, drink and be merry, you’re in for a treat here, it’s approach road are sprinkled with bustling cafés, lively, dog-friendly pubs, and popular independent shops. The fresh veg from Newington Green Fruit & Vegetables. The north-east London postcode is high in demand and is awash with creativity, boutique shops and the latest restaurants.

Church Street is full of artisan coffee shops and smart cafés every few yards including Caffeine London; The Good Egg; The Blue Legume; The Green Room and The Last Crumb Café. There is a wide choice of restaurants including Franco Manca chain pizzeria; Fanny’s Kebabs, now with three branches; Spanish restaurant Black Pig with White Pearls; The Haberdashery for brunch and lunch; Yum Yum, a long-standing modern Thai restaurant in a fine Georgian house.

Clissold Park is a 55acre community park that has tennis courts, a bowling green, ornamental lakes, an aviary and an animal enclosure with deer, goats and chickens, as well as an attractive cafe at the 18th century Grade II listed Clissold House. There is a woodland park and nature reserve at Abney Park Cemetery, where entry is free, and there are lots of activities on offer, from wooden spoon carving to guided nature walks. Both Rectory Road and Canonbury stations are close by offering excellent transport links into central London and beyond.

description:
This handsome classic1920's semi has a hint of Arts and Crafts about it with its mock Tudor gable, twin bay windows and arched covered entrance porch, typical of interwar building styles of the period.
The front garden has raised flowerbeds with mature shrubs edged in Cotswold stone. Guest parking can usually be accomplished as there are no parking restrictions in the top portion of Connaught Avenue, and one vehicle can be parked on the drive and another across the dropped kerb.
Accommodation extends to close to 1700 square ft of well laid out living space over three floors. The house has a characterful feel throughout and on the ground floor we have a welcoming entrance hallway with a handy understairs guest w/c. To the front, a tranquil reception room with plenty of natural light pouring in from its large bay window. The North facing front room provides a cool haven on hot summer days, however the repro 1930’s fireplace is fully functional with a new fireback fitted so a cosy atmosphere can be provided on special occasions. A gas point was also installed to allow it’s replacement by a gas fire.
The hallway gives way to a sociable, open plan kitchen/diner with a semi-circular breakfast bar with another seating area. The work tops, breakfast bar and splash backs are surfaced with “Angola Blue” a Blue flecked Black Granite, the garden is highly visible through generous aluminium windows and tall bi-fold door set.
The porcelain tiled floor in the kitchen diner has a dual zone wet underfloor heating system with very high levels of insulation installed. A new underfloor heating manifold and pump was installed when the Garden room was completed. Overhead is an acoustic ceiling with a twin circuit of dimmable downlights and two loudspeakers powered by a DAB radio. There are two other lighting circuits in the kitchen.
From here we can step out into the bespoke timber framed garden room which combines the light and openness of a traditional conservatory, with a much more contemporary architectural feel to it. Exposed structural timber beams support a hardwood roof which is capped by a specialist drained aluminium glazing system for the triple glazed panels. The roof glazing features architectural glass designed to reduce summer overheating and external noise while providing an excellent view.
Full 2.5 metre height triple panel Visoglide plus sliding glazed doors overlook the garden, while a further 3 Metre hardwood bifold 5 door set opens out onto the sideway allowing further flexibility and making for an impressive entertaining space. Green principles were incorporated into the design to minimise heat loss through the floor and maximise comfort levels by storing daylight solar gain within a thermal floor slab.
A wet underfloor heating system is installed over very high levels of underfloor insulation including foamed glass blocks, allowing all year use. The panelling and skirting boards in the Conservatory include restored genuine antique Teak and Mahogany rescued from a Builders Offices in Buckhurst Hill. A hardwearing floor of large format cream coloured porcelain tiles provides a practical entrance to the garden. Lighting is provided by two separate dimmable LED circuits that can be remotely controlled using Varilight V-PRO Multipoint dimmers and remotes.
The garden extends to just under 100' in length and is south facing, mainly laid to lawn, though it features an area of drained AstroTurf to provide a level games area currently used for an outdoor Table Tennis table and a Wooden children’s play shed. A small aluminium greenhouse and two metal sheds provide ample storage. There are three garden sheds, one with a power supply. There are also large mature trees to the end and side of the garden that provide welcome shade to the astro turf and part of the lawn in summer.
On the first floor there are three good sized bedrooms, two of which are doubles and a modern three piece family bathroom. Lastly, on the top floor is the full-size loft extension with its large double bedroom with fitted storage, full height Juliet style door set balcony with wrought iron balustrade providing wonderful views over the garden and it also has its own well-appointed shower room with w/c.
The room features a double Velux window facing north with one window being a top hung window while the other is a remote-controlled electric window. A further electric window is installed in the loft stairwell to provide ventilation. on and sensor updating, currently Velux automation is restricted to rain sensors with an auto close function.

It's a Mecca for walkers, cyclists and runners using the network of leafy trails that weave their way through these ancient woods. The Royal Forest Hotel, Queen Elizabeth Hunting Lodge and Connaught Water are all within Walking distance as are several golf courses.

Introduction:
Tucked away on the South Downs National Park and yet only ten minutes to the centre of Brighton, Conifers is a wonderfully peaceful retreat offering the rare balance of countryside living with exceptional connectivity. Internally, the property offers a versatile layout with two kitchen–living areas and two well-proportioned double bedrooms. In recent years it has been thoughtfully renovated by owners with a keen eye for sustainability as well as design, creating interiors that balance contemporary style with comfort and practicality.
Set within approximately two acres of land, the property currently comprises a beautifully renovated two/three-bedroom bungalow finished to a high standard throughout, while the generous grounds present exciting potential for further development, subject to the necessary planning consents.
Equally suited to equestrian use, the land has been thoughtfully arranged with three stables, paddocks for grazing and sand school (30 m x 16m / 98 ft x 52 ft), creating an ideal environment for housing ponies or horses. Surrounded by the rolling landscapes of the Downs and enjoying far-reaching views across the countryside, this unique property offers a lifestyle opportunity rarely found so close to Brighton, with easy access to both the A23 for London and the A27 along the south coast.
Exterior & Entrance Hall:
Entirely unique, this single-storey residence occupies its own peaceful setting on Sweet Hill, accessed from Waterhall Road. Approaching from London Road beneath the bridge, the landscape quickly opens out as the rolling South Downs rise around you, with neat hedgerows guiding the way to the generous driveway at Conifers. Here there is ample parking across the forecourt and within the garage.
From the outside, the house appears modest, yet it unfolds to reveal more than 2,000 sq. ft. of flexible living space. As a detached property sharing the quiet lane with just one neighbouring home, it enjoys an exceptional sense of peace and privacy. Windows on all sides draw in natural light and frame views of the surrounding countryside, enhancing the calm atmosphere throughout.
Stepping through the front door, a spacious entrance hall provides a welcoming introduction, complete with an adjoining boot and tack room offering excellent storage for outdoor and equestrian equipment. Polished concrete flooring flows seamlessly through the home, creating a sense of cohesion while pairing beautifully with the soft palette of pale greys and crisp white walls. With boots off, coats hung and riding gear stored away, the first reception room invites you to unwind beside the warmth of the wood-burning stove.
Reception Room One:
Bright and airy, with two casement windows framing leafy views, this calming space offers room for both formal dining alongside the kitchen and comfortable seating arranged around the wood-burning stove. Running neatly along the rear wall, the kitchen is finished in crisp white cabinetry, incorporating a range cooker and space for freestanding appliances, creating a practical yet understated backdrop to the room.
As one of two open-plan reception spaces within the home, this arrangement offers excellent versatility. It would lend itself particularly well to multi-generational living or, if desired, could form part of a self-contained area suitable for holiday letting or a long-term rental, providing potential for additional income.
Family Room & Reception Room Two:
From the first reception room, double doors open through to a bright family or garden room where a wall of glazing frames the garden and allows the outdoors to become part of the living space. Beyond this lies the second reception room, arranged in a similar open-plan style with a streamlined kitchen, space for dining and a comfortable seating area gathered around a contemporary wood-burning stove.
Together, these interconnected rooms offer exceptional flexibility, providing areas for relaxation, entertaining, hobbies or a playroom for younger family members. Filled with natural light throughout the day, they are spaces to be enjoyed in every season, though they come into their own during the warmer months when the garden becomes a natural extension of the home. This side of the house also has its own front entrance, allowing it to be completely self-contained, and both living spaces have independent access to the utility room from the front patio.
Principal Bedroom Suite & Study/Dressing Room:
From the first reception room, a door opens into a bright study where a deep bow window frames tranquil, private views across the garden. Adjoining this space is the larger of the two bedroom suites, a beautifully proportioned room with French doors opening directly onto the garden.
The suite enjoys sole access to a gleaming en suite bathroom, thoughtfully designed with a contemporary interpretation of a classic period style. Here, a freestanding roll-top clawfoot bath sits alongside a separate rainfall shower lined in distinctive brick tiling, creating a space that balances character with modern comfort. Generous in scale, the bedroom allows for a variety of furniture arrangements, while the adjoining study could easily be reimagined as a dressing room or walk-in wardrobe if desired.
Second Bedroom Suite:
Mirroring the style and generous proportions of the first bedroom, the second bedroom suite also enjoys French doors opening directly onto the garden. During the warmer months, this allows you to wake to birdsong and step outside to enjoy a quiet morning coffee on the patio, or later unwind with a drink as the sun sets in the west beyond the hillside.
The suite is further enhanced by a spacious walk-in wardrobe offering ample storage for clothes and shoes, while the adjoining bathroom is finished in a contemporary style with a deep bath and shower above, creating a comfortable and well-appointed private retreat.
Outside Spaces & Outbuildings:
At the rear of the house, a neat paved terrace provides the perfect setting for alfresco dining and relaxed entertaining. Steps rise to a spa pool hot tub for year-round enjoyment before leading onto a secluded lawn bordered by a selection of mature fruit trees which cast welcome dappled shade during the summer months. Beyond, the garden gently climbs the hillside with sweeping areas of lawn and established trees whose spring blossom and nesting branches attract a wealth of wildlife, creating a wonderfully natural setting.
To one side of this open ground sit several useful outbuildings which form the heart of the property’s equestrian facilities. Three buildings currently provide stabling for up to two horses, while two additional structures offer generous space for machinery, tack storage and feed. For those not requiring equestrian use, these buildings also present excellent potential for alternative uses or conversion, subject to the necessary permissions.
Continuing up the hill, the land levels out to reveal a fenced riding arena laid with sand (30 m x 16m / 98 ft x 52 ft), providing an ideal space for schooling, training and everyday exercise. Together with the surrounding paddocks and immediate access to the Downland landscape, the grounds offer a superb and highly practical environment for those with horses or ponies.
Owner’s thoughts
“We have truly loved the space and freedom this home has given us, which we created as two linked living areas to suit our lifestyle. It is wonderfully peaceful here, yet incredibly well connected by road, and there are beautiful footpaths leading straight onto the South Downs which we have enjoyed exploring throughout the decade we have lived here. As equestrians, it has been the perfect setting for both us and our ponies, with the land and facilities working beautifully for day-to-day life. It’s a very special place, and we hope the next owners will enjoy the lifestyle it offers just as much as we have.”
Education
Primary: Patcham Primary School, Westdene Primary School Secondary: Patcham High School, Cardinal Newman RC Private: roughly within 30 mins - Brighton College, Brighton Girls, Roedean School, Lancing College, Lewes Old Grammar School, Hurstpierpoint College
Location Guide
It is little wonder that so many families are choosing to move from the city centre to Patcham and its surrounding countryside on the South Downs National Park. Here, homes and gardens are more generous, parking is readily available, and children can grow up within a welcoming, family-focused community where they can play safely and neighbours know one another. While the setting feels wonderfully peaceful, the city remains easily accessible with regular transport links in and out, and the surrounding landscape offers an abundance of mature trees, scenic footpaths, countryside walks and traditional pubs quite literally on the doorstep. For commuters, the A23 provides a direct route to London, while Preston Park Station is also within easy reach for rail connections. The nearby A27 offers convenient access east towards Lewes and west along the South Coast. Closer to home, Preston Village provides a charming selection of local amenities including independent shops, an award-winning bakery, welcoming cafés, restaurants and a post office. Meanwhile, the vibrant city of Brighton & Hove lies just ten minutes away by car, offering theatres, cinemas, museums and, of course, the iconic seafront and beach.

Between leafy Dyke Road Park and the open acres of Preston Park with easy access to the sea as well as into or out of the city, this is one of the most desirable areas of our vibrant city. The Entrance Hall:
This stately house with immediate appeal has unique architectural detail and the impressive entrance (with a side gate for bikes) is reached through a front garden planted for privacy and scent. Inside has a stylish commitment to style, comfort and practicality and it begins in the entrance lobby with rush matting underfoot and intricate plasterwork overhead opens to a hushed hallway with a guest w.c. tucked away and solid wood floorboards which continues through into the living dining room for an easy flow.

Built in an age reliant on natural light, sunlight streams through a beautifully proportioned living dining room which has been opened to create an inviting space ideal for entertaining or family time. At the top of stairs lushly carpeted with thick underlay so you won’t hear a thing, the first of the bedrooms is bright and cheerful with inspiring garden views. On the first landing, with 3.56 x 3.75m (11’8 x 12’3) it is lined with bespoke wardrobes making it the perfect dressing room or a generous bedroom for a teenager, visitor or an au-pair where the occupants can come and go without disturbing the main bedrooms - and the bonus is that it is next to the luxury bathroom.
With a classic high end finish the pale grey and marble bathroom by Fired Earth is light and airy with a dual head shower above the designer bathtub which includes a shelf with downlighters to highlight the feature tiles, natural light, a warming rail for towels, underfloor heating, inset mirrored unit with hidden charge points and a glamorous lit mirror above the Duravit hand basin which has a stylish vanity unit beneath it.

The First Floor Bedroom and Principal Room:
Up a few steps, the second double bedroom has plenty of character and space of its own with a period fireplace, 3.26 x 3.62m (10’8 x 11’10) to spread your wings and garden views.

At the front of the house, the wonderful principal bedroom spans the full width of this substantial property with 5.04 x 4.58m (16’7 x 15’0) in which to unwind. With the restful proportions only a period home can deliver, a handsome, Victorian fireplace with framing, fitted wardrobes and romantic floral frieze, the decoration is in soothing historic hues and a broad bay window as well as tall window with shutters almost fill the front wall to flood the room with light and frame the tree, obliquely outside, which provides shelter for little birds.

The Top Floor Double Bedrooms, One En-Suite:
Blissfully quiet at the top of the house, the spacious bedroom at the back is a serene sanctuary with new oak flooring underfoot. Light pours through the large picture window with views over a sea of gardens and it is used at present as a comfortable place in which to work from home. Originally designed as an alternative principal bedroom, there is 3.28 x 3.79m (10’9 x 12’5) to enjoy.

At the front, with an unusual, smoothly curved bay, a beautiful precursor to the later Art Deco style, the sunny fifth bedroom has open views and fitted wardrobes to fill. In winter, there are glimpses to the rooftop of outstanding BHASVIC 6th Form College and the chic en-suite bathroom beneath a Velux has a designer finish.

The house is warm in winter, airy in summer and the garden is private and peaceful – and the apple tree gives us all the fruit we need! This is a great place to live with a friendly community, considerate neighbours who have become friends and the al fresco lifestyle of 7 Dials – and its 7 ways to the entire city – is a 3 minute drive, or under 10 mins on foot. description:
Contemporary coastal living with breath-taking sea views
A striking, individually designed five-bedroom detached home occupying an elevated position on one of Saltdean’s most desirable residential roads. Bold architecture, beautifully individual interiors and an ingenious reverse-level arrangement combine to create a home that feels unmistakably different.
From the street, the house immediately sets its stall out. Crisp rendered elevations, contemporary cladding, dark-framed glazing and an asymmetric roofline give it a distinctive architectural presence, while the broad frontage provides off-road parking alongside the integral garage. Above, glass-fronted balconies hint at what really defines this house: light, outlook and the sea. Solar panels are discreetly integrated into the roof, adding an energy-conscious element to the property while complementing its contemporary architectural character.
The accommodation has been deliberately arranged to make the most of its elevated setting, with the principal living space occupying the first floor. It is here that the house becomes something genuinely special.
A spectacular vaulted kitchen, dining and living room forms the social heart of the home. The soaring ceilings and extensive glazing create an extraordinary sense of volume, while large doors draw the eye beyond the room towards the balcony, surrounding green space and stunning outlook.
The kitchen has been designed with character rather than convention. Rich green cabinetry, pale worktops and warm metallic accents sit alongside open timber shelving and abundant planting, while the substantial island is wrapped in reclaimed timber laid in a distinctive chevron pattern. Sculptural suspended lighting and a dramatic stainless-steel extractor create a sophisticated architectural focal point above.
There is space here to cook, dine, entertain and relax without any part of the room feeling compromised. The sitting area naturally gravitates towards the glazing, where doors open onto the broad balcony and transform the room during warmer months. It is a wonderfully sociable space, but equally compelling when the house is quiet and the changing coastal outlook becomes the focus.
The first floor also provides two generous bedrooms. The principal bedroom enjoys its own en-suite shower room, while an additional WC serves the second bedroom and living accommodation. This arrangement gives the upper floor an appealing degree of independence and places the principal sleeping accommodation alongside the best views in the house.
The ground floor reveals just how versatile the property is. Three further double bedrooms provide excellent accommodation for children, guests or multigenerational living, with one benefitting from its own en suite shower room. One of the bedrooms could equally be reimagined as a substantial study, gym or second reception room, offering exceptional flexibility to suit a range of lifestyles.
The family bathroom is full of personality, combining deep green walls with traditional-style sanitaryware, a freestanding roll-top bath and separate glazed shower. Elsewhere, the interiors continue to avoid the predictable, with another beautifully finished shower room introducing soft blush tones, patterned stone-effect flooring and warm brass detailing.
Practicality has not been forgotten, but even the utility spaces have been conceived with entertaining and everyday living in mind. A discreetly fitted hall cupboard has been designed to house the washing machine and tumble dryer, keeping laundry appliances neatly tucked away and freeing the additional ground-floor space for something rather more sociable.
Known within the house as the ‘Snug’, this versatile room was designed as a second lounge, combining comfortable living space with useful cabinetry and integrated appliances. Bi-fold doors open directly onto the garden, creating a seamless connection between the room and outside space and making it particularly well suited to summer entertaining, family gatherings or simply relaxing with the garden beyond.
The integral garage offers useful parking and storage, while the solar panels provide an additional practical benefit, contributing to the home's energy efficiency and reinforcing its thoughtful contemporary credentials.
Outside, the detached garden office adds another valuable dimension. Completely separate from the main house, it lends itself perfectly to home working, a creative studio or a quiet retreat without sacrificing a bedroom.
But ultimately, this house is about its relationship with its surroundings. The elevated balcony becomes an extension of the living room, overlooking open green space and carrying the view towards the coast. With relatively little between the house and the horizon, the outlook has an unusually open quality. The sea is not simply glimpsed from an upstairs window; it forms part of the everyday backdrop to the home.
Individual, substantial and refreshingly unconventional, Arundel Drive East offers the space of a serious family house with the atmosphere of a contemporary coastal retreat, complemented by solar panels and thoughtful modern design, and is offered with no onward chain

Nestled on the leafy fringes of the city, on the cusp of picturesque parkland incorporating miles of cycle tracks and footpaths, and with renowned schooling within easy reach, No. 18, Stevenson Crescent offers all the hallmarks of family living before ever setting foot through the door.
A modern home, with an elegant, contemporary architectural design, characterised by large windows, tall ceilings and light-filled spaces, No. 18 is a home designed for 21st century living.
Ample parking for three cars, a luxury in a city location, is accompanied by a garage with EV charging point which can easily accommodate a large car or SUV.
Into the light
Indoors, in the entrance hall, the high ceilings and abundance of natural light amplify the airy and open feel of the home immediately. Interior design-led décor defines each space, with the panelled walls adding to the characterful feel of the home, whilst underfoot, herringbone Karndean flooring flows out.
Store coats and shoes in the cupboard beneath the stairs, while to the immediate left of the front door, in the sitting room, shades of Farrow and Ball’s Olive dress the walls and bespoke library and media unit, ambiently illuminated by integrated lighting. Minimal frames to the large window panes in the box bay give an almost flush, modern finish, flooding the room with light whilst framing views out over the park. Spacious and serene, whether enjoying a quiet afternoon leafing through a book or a lively evening with friends, this sitting room offers the ideal setting for any occasion.
Follow the effortless flow of the home through to the open plan kitchen-dining-living room ahead from the entrance, where views of the garden are captured via French doors opening out to a private patio, perfect for al fresco dining throughout the summer.
Family time
Wine and dine at the table, with instant access outdoors for summer barbecues, or gather at the sociable breakfast bar for morning coffee and crumpets whilst catching up on family plans for the day ahead. Crisp countertops provide plenty of preparation space, with ample storage nestled within the cabinetry, while high performing appliances include a Siemens double oven and grill, a dishwasher, five-burner gas hob and fridge freezer.
Nestled off the kitchen, keep the laundry at bay in the utility room, where a Bosch tumble dryer and washing machine can be found. Smart heating, a feature throughout the home, allows you to set the ideal temperature via the electric thermostat, which automatically activates when the room falls below your chosen setting. A handy wash room with WC and basin can also be found off the utility room.
On the first floor, light streams in through the large double-height windows above the front door and the skylight above the stairs.
Soak and sleep
Light and bright, the guest bedroom on the right basks in beautiful views out over the greenery to the front, where the park extends, dotted with mature trees – a haven for nature. Decorated in neutral shades, there is ample storage in the built-in wardrobes, while a shower room en suite offers instant refreshment.
A second bedroom, to the right, is a peaceful retreat, currently serving as a home office, though still a spacious double.
Fully tiled and furnished with a bath containing overhead shower, wash basin, WC and heated towel radiator, the family bathroom offers refreshment for all, situated directly opposite the stairs.
Turning right from the bathroom, enchanting, hand-painted murals to the walls in the third of the double bedrooms evoke a fairytale feel in the nursery, another beautifully light double overlooking the garden.
Sense the serenity in the principal suite, with its soaring, vaulted ceiling and private balcony overlooking the leafy views of the park to the front. Cosy, yet spacious, dressed in dreamy shades of Farrow and Ball’s Green Smoke, this sophisticated bedroom is a true sanctuary, brimming with storage in the built-in, mirrored wardrobes.
Refresh and revive in the spacious en suite, furnished with bath and walk-in shower. Additional storage can also be found in the airing cupboard on the landing.
Garden
Outside, the south-facing garden is made for relaxed outdoor living, with a sunny patio directly opening up from the dining-kitchen perfect for barbecues and long summer evenings, while a wide stretch of lawn provides space for children and pets to run and play. Set back and secure, this is an outdoor space where families can unwind and make memories.
Out and about
Discover all that the local area has to offer close by. With its welcoming, international community, Headington is home to many medics and academics thanks to its proximity to the city’s hospitals and universities.
Comfortably commutable to Oxford city centre (so much so the home qualifies for permits under the Oxford traffic filters), enjoy all the culture, cafes and convenience the city has to offer before returning home to the quiet calm of No. 18 and its verdant parkside setting.
Families are well served by excellent independent schools and nurseries, while the John Radcliffe Hospital is within walking distance – ideal for those working there.
Summertown and Headington’s high streets are nearby, offering a wide range of shops, cafés and amenities, while road links make travel further afield effortless. For London commuters, Oxford Parkway station is just a short drive away, with speedy services into the capital.
But the emerald jewel in No. 18’s crown is its leafy surrounds, with green space abounding on the doorstep, perfect for walking and cycling. From the front door wander through local parks or head out to nearby Waterperry Gardens and Port Meadow for longer walks in beautiful surroundings.
Food lovers are spoiled for choice, with a great mix of independent eateries in Headington itself, the stylish cafés and restaurants of Summertown and the vibrant dining scene at Oxford’s Westgate Shopping Centre.
Blending contemporary design with family-friendly comfort and an unrivalled location, No. 18, Stevenson Crescent is a home perfectly placed for both city living and parkland escapes.

The bicycle and pedestrian-friendly routes in and out of Oxford city, including the bypass routes and the canal towpath add variety and options for a local commuter. Commuting by road, there is the A40, A34, A420, A44 and M40.

A charming 3-storey, bay-fronted semi-detached home that’s undergone thoughtful refurbishment by the current owners, with rear extension and loft conversion. Ideally located for families in a quiet cul-de-sac in a sought-after neighbourhood with easy access to local amenities, the accommodation is arranged over three floors and balances 1930s period detail with the effortless flow of modern living.

On entering the home, you are struck by the beautifully tiled entrance hall which leads to a bay fronted south facing reception room with original 1930s fireplace. The contemporary kitchen sits in the middle of the house with an open plan dining/family area adjacent, with ceiling lantern and French doors opening onto the rear garden. A very useful family bathroom and separate utility space completes the lower level.

The first floor has two double bedrooms, a single bedroom and a second family bathroom, with stairs leading to a bright, attractive loft room with ensuite and a Juliette balcony with sweeping views of the area.

The front and rear gardens are laid to lawn with well-stocked herbaceous borders. The property also benefits from an attractive, insulated garden office/studio with wood-burning stove.

Location:
The property is located just on the outskirts of Iffley Village, which has retained a unique village feel, despite being only two miles south of the city centre. Its leafy roads, varied architecture and active local community make it a truly unique suburb of Oxford.

Iffley offers a Norman church, well-patronised community village shop, two public houses and two hotels. After crossing Iffley Lock, the Thames towpath offers a delightful walk or cycle ride past water meadows and the university boathouses to Folly Bridge and central Oxford.

The city centre is also easily accessible by car, and there is a frequent bus service along nearby Iffley Road. Oxford Station provides regular rail services to London Paddington in 55 minutes, and the Oxford Tube bus also runs frequent services to London Victoria in 90 minutes.

“Welcome to our much-loved family home. Tucked away in a quiet cul-de-sac, it has been the perfect sanctuary for raising our two children and we are sure it will be just as special to its next owners.

One thing we have really appreciated is the unique warmth of the neighbourhood. It’s a friendly, sociable, and close-knit community where neighbours truly look out for one another. Inside, the house balances spacious comfort with a warm, inviting atmosphere, offering plenty of room for a growing family to thrive. The open plan kitchen and living area is truly the heart of the home—we’ve spent countless hours gathered around the table or enjoying drinks on the balcony overlooking the garden. The separate sitting room catches the evening glow, making it a cosy place to unwind after a long day—and when nights draw in there’s nothing like lighting a fire in the original tiled hearth.

We’ve restored and extended the home, balancing original features such as the mosaic tiled entryway and stained glass top lights while opening up the space to bring in more light and flow for modern family living. The recently converted loft is a highlight, featuring private ensuite and elevated, far-reaching views of the Oxford skyline.

Keen gardeners, we’ve enjoyed tending to the front and rear borders where established shrubs give the garden shape during winter, and perennials add bursts of seasonal colour.

We have loved our time here and are sad to leave such wonderful neighbours, but we are excited to pass this beautiful home on to a new family who will appreciate and care for these walls as much as we have.”

A Cottage with Character, a Kitchen to Love & a Summer House to Escape To!

Brook End Road South, Chelmer Village, Chelmsford | Three-Bedroom Semi-Detached Cottage

Some homes are all about the modern finish, others are full of character… and then there are those rare finds that give you the best of both worlds!

Believed to date back to before 1900, this charming three-bedroom semi-detached cottage is packed with personality, blending period charm with contemporary touches in all the right places. Think exposed brickwork, a cosy feature fireplace, a gorgeous shaker-style kitchen and even a summer house with electricity. Yes, really! Whether you're searching for somewhere to put down roots, a home with a little more individuality or simply a property that makes you say "oh, I love that!", this one deserves your attention.

Let's step inside...

The Lounge – Old-School Charm Meets Cosy Nights In

First up, a lounge with bags of character! The exposed brickwork brings texture and warmth to the room, giving it that lovely cottage feel that's difficult to replicate. Add in the feature electric fireplace and you've got the perfect spot for cosy evenings, a good film and a blanket you probably won't want to share.

And it's not just about the character. Three windows allow plenty of natural light to flood the room, keeping the space bright and welcoming. It's the kind of lounge that feels equally suited to lazy Sunday mornings and evenings spent entertaining friends.

The Kitchen/Diner – Shaker Style & Breakfast Bar Goals

Now, this is where things get exciting!

The kitchen/diner features a stylish Wren shaker-style kitchen, offering timeless good looks that complement the cottage's traditional character beautifully. It's a lovely combination of classic styling and modern practicality, proving that you really can have the best of both worlds.

Integrated appliances include a washing machine and dishwasher, because nobody wants to spend their evening washing up when there's a sofa calling their name!

The limestone tiled flooring adds a natural, elegant finish, while the fabulous breakfast bar is a real highlight. Morning coffee, quick lunches, a catch-up with friends or a little something while dinner is cooking… this is one of those features that quickly becomes the heart of the home.

And there's more! A skylight brings additional natural light into the space, creating a bright and airy atmosphere. Stylish, practical and full of charm, this kitchen/diner is ready for everything from everyday family life to weekend entertaining.

The First Floor – Three Bedrooms & Room to Make It Your Own

Heading upstairs, you'll find three bedrooms, offering plenty of flexibility for modern living.

The Principal Bedroom – Your Own Little Retreat

The main bedroom benefits from its own shower en-suite, adding a welcome touch of convenience and privacy. No more morning bathroom queues or negotiating who gets ready first!

It's a comfortable space to unwind at the end of the day, with the added bonus of having your own en-suite facilities.

Bedroom Two & Bedroom Three – Room for Whatever Life Throws Your Way

The two additional bedrooms offer plenty of possibilities. Need rooms for the family? A guest bedroom for visitors? A home office for those working-from-home days? Or perhaps a hobby room for that interest you keep promising to make more time for? The choice is yours.

A separate family bathroom completes the first-floor accommodation, providing additional convenience for the household and guests.

The Garden – Low Maintenance, High Enjoyment

Fancy a garden without sacrificing every sunny weekend to mowing the lawn? This could be right up your street!

The rear garden features artificial grass for a neat, low-maintenance finish, giving you more time to relax and less time worrying about the garden looking presentable. Whether it's a morning coffee in the sunshine, a few drinks with friends or simply enjoying some fresh air after a busy day, there's plenty of potential to make this outdoor space your own.

And Then There's the Summer House...

Because apparently, this home wasn't finished showing off!

The garden benefits from a summer house with electricity, offering a fantastic additional space with plenty of possibilities. A home office away from the distractions of the main house? A creative studio? A hobby room? Or simply somewhere to escape for a little peace and quiet?

Whatever you choose, having electricity already in place makes this a particularly appealing feature. Just imagine having your own little hideaway at the end of the garden!

Driveway Parking – One Less Thing to Worry About

The property also benefits from driveway parking, providing valuable off-road parking and adding to the everyday practicality of this charming home.

Why This Cottage Stands Out

What makes this property so appealing is its individuality. The characterful exposed brickwork and traditional cottage feel sit beautifully alongside the contemporary Wren kitchen, integrated appliances and en-suite shower room.

It's not trying to be a brand-new, cookie-cutter home, and that's exactly the point! It has history, personality and features that give it a real sense of identity, while still offering the modern comforts we all appreciate.

The Final Word

A charming cottage with character, a kitchen you'll want to show off and a summer house that could become your favourite place to work, create or simply escape for a little peace and quiet.

With three bedrooms, a stylish kitchen/diner, a characterful lounge, en-suite facilities, driveway parking and a low-maintenance garden, this lovely home on Brook End Road South, Chelmer Village, offers a wonderful blend of old and new.

Whether you're a couple looking for somewhere with personality, a family needing flexible space or a buyer who appreciates a home with a story to tell, this could be the one that steals your heart.

Character? Absolutely. Modern comforts? You bet. A summer house with electricity? Now we're talking!

Chelmsford is a vibrant and highly sought-after city in Essex, offering an appealing mix of city living, green open spaces and excellent commuter connections. With a bustling High Street, a fantastic selection of shops, cafés, restaurants, bars and leisure facilities, there is plenty to enjoy, whether you're looking for a relaxed coffee stop, a spot of retail therapy or an evening out with friends. The popular Bond Street development, alongside High Chelmer and The Meadows shopping centres, provides a varied shopping experience, while the city's regular markets and cultural attractions add to its welcoming atmosphere. For those who enjoy the outdoors, Central Park offers a lovely green retreat in the heart of the city, while the beautiful Hylands Estate provides expansive parkland, woodland walks and a historic house to explore. Families can also enjoy a range of leisure activities, museums and recreational facilities throughout the area. Commuters are particularly well catered for, with regular train services from Chelmsford to London Liverpool Street taking around 35 minutes, alongside convenient road links via the A12. Combining excellent transport links, an extensive range of amenities and plenty of opportunities to enjoy both city life and the outdoors, Chelmsford is an attractive place to call home for first-time buyers, professionals and families alike.
